MECHANISM (answers 'why predict endpos_logp but not emission'): the two DVs are NEARLY INDEPENDENT across bystanders (emission vs endpos_logp Spearman rho=0.09 p=0.65; rho=0.19 over 28 = #456 H3-miss). They capture different LEAK ROUTES:
- endpos_logp = teacher-forced ※ prob at the fixed trained end-slot (\n\n※). Personas geometrically CLOSE to source (data_scientist cos +0.93, helpful_assistant +0.60, pentester +0.61) inherited the trained end-slot habit -> high logp -> cosine/JS/KL correlate.
- emission_rate = ※ anywhere in a free sample, DOMINATED by structured-output contexts (fammate_format_1 cos -0.47 emis 0.22 logp -4.52; fammate_format_2 cos -0.49 emis 0.21) that leak ※ mid-body, are semantically OPPOSITE the source (negative cosine), and have LOW end-slot logp. So they push emission up at negative cosine -> decouple/anti-correlate emission from the predictors (cos->emission rho=-0.24 N=27).
Net: predictors track the persona-similarity / trained-end-slot route (endpos_logp); the behaviorally-dominant leak is a format-structure route orthogonal to persona geometry.
CAVEAT (deflates the logp side): JS/KL-to-source AND endpos_logp are BOTH read off the model's persona-conditioned next-token distributions -> shared-method variance / partly mechanical, not predictor-vs-independent-outcome. emission is a sampled outcome one step removed. Plus emission floor-compressed+noisy (n=160 near 0.04) lowers power. So 'geometry predicts marker leakage' is NOT supported behaviorally; geometry predicts an end-slot logp readout partly coupled to it by construction.
